guidance.inspection: Read each return, destruction, or deletion duty with its governing trigger. Determine whether termination or expiration—not merely a request, rejection, or discretionary option—activates the duty, and retain the protected object, actor, timing, alternatives, exceptions, and necessary list preamble.

Reconstruct the identification rule for every form of protected information. Decide whether every item must be expressly designated by the disclosing party, or whether confidentiality may instead arise from circumstances, subject matter, reasonable understanding, or automatic inclusion. Retain form-specific timing and later written-confirmation requirements.

any_phrases: should know is treated as confidential

guidance.inspection: For each independent-development clause, retain its exception or permission preamble and all no-access, no-use, proof, actor, and timing qualifications. Distinguish actual permission or exclusion for independent development from prior possession, mere product competition, or information received from others.

Locate the operative permission or exception allowing the receiving party's employees to receive protected information. Retain need-to-know, purpose, confidentiality-undertaking, notice, and responsibility conditions. Definitions and employee mentions are contextual leads only unless linked to operative disclosure or access language.

Read each ownership, reservation, no-grant, or licence provision as a complete operative clause. Decide whether the agreement grants any right in Confidential Information, distinguishing access or purpose-limited use from a proprietary licence and accounting for express limited licences or exceptions. Retain independently operative ownership and no-right provisions.

Inspect restrictions concerning the existence, occurrence, status, terms, or public announcement of negotiations, discussions, agreements, or a contemplated transaction. Retain the governing nondisclosure lead-in, consent and audience limitations, exceptions, and every independently responsive list item, excluding siblings about different subject matter.

Collect clauses that expressly continue identified contractual obligations after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, return, or destruction. Retain the affected obligations, trigger, duration, endpoint, exceptions, and governing split text. Distinguish surviving duties from a bare termination right, accrued rights or remedies, and severability language preserving provisions after invalidity.

Read the complete condition tying legal, regulatory, governmental, subpoena, or court compulsion to notice by the receiving party to the disclosing party. Retain permission limits and protective-order steps only as part of that mechanism. Reject unauthorized-use notices and bare compelled-disclosure permissions lacking a notice duty.

Inspect employment or hiring solicitation provisions for the restricted actor, targeted officers, employees, or personnel, duration, approval condition, covered contacts, and exceptions. Follow a matched restriction through its enumerated target classes and qualifications. Do not treat proxy solicitation or a standstill heading as solicitation of the disclosing party's representatives.

Inspect each copying or reproduction provision for actor, protected object, modality, purpose, quantity, consent requirement, and exceptions. A limited permission or necessary-purpose exception may support the hypothesis; an unqualified prohibition or consent condition may oppose it. Do not treat post-return retention as permission to create copies.

Read retention language together with the return or destruction rule it qualifies. Verify that possession is allowed after the applicable return or destruction event, and retain the holder, material, purpose, duration, access limits, continuing confidentiality, and exception preamble. Distinguish permitted archival or legal retention from a command to return all copies.

guidance.inspection: Read the operative protected-information definition and its subject-matter enumeration. Determine whether protection is confined to technical information or also reaches business, financial, marketing, personnel, contact, operational, or other nontechnical material. Do not use unrelated actor or disclosure clauses as definition evidence.

Determine whether orally or verbally conveyed information enters the protected class, including any identification or written-confirmation condition. Retain the operative definition and necessary continuation, but do not treat an oral negotiation reference or a written-only rule as oral inclusion without reading its polarity.

guidance.inspection: Inspect whether similar information may be obtained from a source other than the disclosing party. Retain the exception preamble and provenance, confidentiality-duty, knowledge, lawful-means, and timing qualifications. Do not substitute independent development or merely pursuing discussions with third parties for acquisition of information.

Identify an operative permission, exception, or prohibition governing disclosure or access by nonemployee recipients such as agents, consultants, counsel, advisers, contractors, financing sources, or other representatives. Retain recipient-class definitions only with the operative clause and its need-to-know, purpose, consent, and confidentiality conditions. Employee-only permission may oppose broader third-party sharing.

Inspect operative use restrictions for the receiving actor, protected object, stated purpose, exceptions, and polarity. A sole-purpose rule or prohibition on other uses supports limited use; access, disclosure permission, ownership, or a licence clause alone does not. Retain governing list preambles when the use rule is a split item.
